utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, and good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. This is Tuesday, March 2nd, 2010, and I greet Mr. Seselj, Ms. Biersay, and Mr. Marcussen, as well as their Case Manager, and everyone helping us in this courtroom. We were supposed to hear a witness, but for health reasons, unfortunately, we'll have no witness. However, I believe that we had to have an administrative hearing. Last time, we noticed that we were running short of time and that it's best to deal with housekeeping matters when we have enough time, and that's when we have no witness. As far as I'm concerned, I will first read a decision issued by the Trial Chamber as the -- regarding the time allocation for the next witness, VS-1058, scheduled next week, and he should be here. It's almost sure, 100 per cent. I will also read a dissenting opinion regarding the time allocation. After that, I will review the situation for the six remaining witnesses, calling them by their pseudonym, so that all parties know exactly where we stand. Then I will also deal with the issue of Mr. Seselj's associates through a motion made under Rule 33 bis by the Registrar, as far as lack of financial means is concerned. And then I will give Mr. Seselj the floor for his comments, administrative comments. But first let's deal with the first issue, which has to do with the time allocation regarding the testimony of Witness 1058. Proprio motu, given Article 98 [as interpreted] of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, according to which the Trial Chamber can control the way the witnesses are examined and the way evidence is shown in order to ensure that everything is as efficient as possible, given the consolidated decision on the imposition of a counsel and the postponement -- and the motion of the Prosecution on the additional time of November 23, 2000 [as interpreted], and on the scheduling order of December 8, 2009, in which the Trial Chamber decided that Witness VS-1058 would only be heard for 30 minutes by the Judges and then 30 minutes by each party; given the press statement made by the witness, a statement made by the -- to the investigator of the ICTY on 21 and 22nd April, 2004, and on September 25th, 2006, as well as what the statement made to the accused in 2008; and given that the time allotted for VS-1058 was not sufficient for the Trial Chamber to put all the questions required, therefore confirms the majority rule obtained by the Trial Chamber, with a dissenting opinion by Judge Antonetti, and all this was disclosed to the party on -- and given that the -- all parties will have an hour and 30 minutes for the examination/cross-examination of Witness VS-1058. This is a majority decision, which means that next week Witness VS-1058 will first be heard -- examined by the Judges for an hour and 30 minutes, then by the Prosecution for an hour and 30 minutes, and then by Mr. Seselj for another hour and 30 minutes. As far as I'm concerned, I'm of a dissenting opinion. I believe that 30 minutes was sufficient for this witness, and for which reason -- for these reasons from the decision of November 8, 2008 [as interpreted], the Trial Chamber reduced the indictment. And on paragraph 28, the Trial Chamber mentioned what follows, and I quote: "This being said, the Prosecution can still present evidence that does not have to do with the incriminated facts, but which can back the indictment, without limiting itself to proving that several crimes have occurred, even if this evidence has to do with a crime scene, where no evidence is required." Let me remind you that Witness VS-1058 -- I will not mention his name, but Witness 1058 is going to testify on the recruitment of volunteers, on the speeches made by the accused, on the operations conducted by the SRS volunteers, operations conducted with the Red Berets, operations in the regions of Bosanski Samac with a VRS unit, and as well as the arrest of the group of Lugar and the military police in Bosanski Samac. As you know, Bosanski Samac is a municipality that was deleted from the indictment. Therefore, if the witness comes, he will only testify as to the deliberate conduct of the accused, i.e., Rule 93 of the procedure. The evidence helping to establish a deliberate pattern of conduct can be admitted in the interests of justice. Therefore, the witness will come in order to talk about the recruitment of volunteers, the way they were enrolled, and possibly the action conducted by the SRS on the military theaters. He might possibly talk about this. Therefore, given the number of witnesses that we still have, 30 minutes would have been sufficient for this witness, which is why I am of a dissenting opinion. Now let me briefly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a problem with page 2. There's a mistake. The decision just read by Judge Antonetti is referred, on line 8 -- there's a reference on line 8 to Article 90(F) and not 98. So it's now corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this decision is based on Rule 90(F). Now, as far as the situation of the remaining witnesses is concerned, we still have six witnesses - I'm not going to give their names - VS-1017, 026, VS-034, VS-1058, VS-032, and Witness Isak Gasi. This last witness is not protected. Now, as far as VS-017 is concerned, he was supposed to be heard today. Unfortunately, because of his health, he cannot come. First, we'll check, of course, what his health situation is. The Trial Chamber has a number of measures that it can take to do that. So either the witness will be in a position to testify soon enough or he will not be able to, or maybe he could testify through a videolink. And the Trial Chamber will make a decision once it has a medical record in its hands. 026 now. VS-026 was supposed to be heard on January 19 and 20, 2010. For medical reasons, he was unable to come. Therefore, on February 17th, 2010, we asked for a medical examination to take place. And once we have the feedback, we will determine what we'll do. Now, Witness 034, VS-034. He was scheduled for February 9 and 10, 2010. He also has health problems. We had provided for a videolink possibly, and on February 11th we asked for a medical examination to be conducted. And as soon as we have the feedback, there again, we will rule on this. Now, Witness VS-1058, I mentioned him earlier. He is scheduled for March 9. Mr. Isak Gasi is scheduled for March 10. And we have the last one, VS-32. He was supposed to be heard on February 23rd and 24th. By decision, he was supposed to testify by videolink, but for medical reasons he was unable to attend. So we asked also for another medical examination to be carried out. We asked for that on January 6th, 2010. And normally, if everything runs correctly, he should be heard on May 4th and 5th, 2010. The problem is that out of these six, we have three people who are really ill, and we don't know whether, in the end, they'll be able to testify. And we need medical records in order to make a decision on all this. That's the situation as it is now. When we made our scheduling order, we thought that we had January, February, and March to finish off these witnesses, but now we're running late, unfortunately. But we cannot be blamed for running late. Mr. Seselj, unfortunately, you are dependent on the health situation of these witnesses, just like us. As you know, the Trial Chamber wants to hear them as soon as possible, but there's not much we can do right now. Now, lastly, before I give you the floor, as you know, that in the decision, the date of which I forgot, we said that Mr. Krasic could come to The Hague, and we had decided that his expenses would be paid for by the Registrar. But the Registry, a few days ago, sent us a few submissions, which I'm sure you received, if they were translated. In these submissions, the Registrar noted our decision but is sending the ball into our camp, saying that the Registrar can only implement the decision if you can really prove that you have no financial means. When I read all these submissions, I was a bit flabbergasted, I must say. Why is that? This dates back -- this is a very old problem. It dates back ages ago. The Registry's position, which is absolutely normal, is that it will only pay for counsel or for associates if the accused is destitute. As far as you're concerned, you had given us documents which obviously the Registrar does not find suitable. I have thought about this over the weekend, and I thought the following, and I want this on the transcript: If you had asked for counsel, then there would be no problem. You would be given a counsel, a co-counsel, and an entire team of assistants; and this would cost hundreds of thousands of Euros. Now, you don't want a counsel, and you could have been appointed a stand-by counsel. That's also costly, but there the Registrar is ready to pay for that. However, because you are defending yourself, you're not entitled to anything unless you can prove that you're totally destitute. Now, I don't know how things occur in the Karadzic case, but I note that Mr. Karadzic has associates, legal associates. Apparently, they're paid. I don't know whether Mr. Karadzic is destitute or not. But as far as he's concerned, obviously, he's not running into any problems. He gets what he wants, and you're not getting anything. Now, this is what I propose to the Trial Chamber, and if they don't agree with me, I'll do it on my own. I would suggest that we send a letter to the minister in charge of co-operation with this Tribunal to ask him to seise the competent ministry, as far as fiscal issues are concerned, so that we can know whether your fiscal situation in Serbia is such that you are poor, rich, destitute. And once we get -- all I can do, of course, is first seise this agency in charge of co-operation, but it's always been very helpful. But when we have the answer of this ministry, I will have a better opinion and also the Trial Chamber will have a better opinion of your wealth situation, because if you have wealth in Serbia, the Tax Administration must know about this, if you have property. If you have bank accounts, also, they must know about this. If you have a car, a yacht - I don't know what you may have - they must know. And they will be able to tell us exactly what your financial situation is like. And then I will send this letter to the Registrar for his information. However, even if you were not destitute, if we found out that you were not destitute, that you had -- that you were extremely wealthy, that your income is huge, you know, compared to wages in your country, and you are a university professor, I mean a university professor is not usually a very wealthy man, but even if you're an extremely well-paid university professor, I believe that the cost of defending yourself in a tribunal, in an international tribunal, are out of proportion for anyone. Even for someone that has sufficient revenue to live can't face to such expenses, and therefore the Registry and the funds of the Tribunal must contribute to your Defence. So, to sum up, I'm very surprised to see that you are said to be destitute, that you have to prove that you're destitute, and that right now you cannot obtain anything; whereas Mr. Karadzic obviously is not running into any problem to get financial help. So I believe that there is double standards being used here, and I wonder why. And I'm saying this in front of my fellow Judge, who is also sitting in the Karadzic case, and I hope that she will support my opinion, as well as Judge Harhoff. But you have to be able to defend yourself, Mr. Seselj. I must tell you that I was very surprised when you told us that you would not appeal the decision for a stay because you did not have your associates. It's true that you did not make a certification of appeal, and the whole trial was postponed for a while. And I thought that -- here I decided that -- I thought that this must be a problem. Maybe this was a tactic on your side. But, anyway, you told us that you were not certifying for appeal because you didn't have your associates, and as a result, well, the trial was postponed for almost a year. And we lost a year. So as far as your associates are concerned, I will ask my -- I will suggest to my colleagues that we officially seise the competent Serbian authority so that we know exactly what your financial situation is like. To sum things up, this morning I was looking at the Rules of Procedure and Evidence on -- of the ICC on this question of financial aid and legal aid, and I noted that at the ICC the Trial Chamber has control over this, and the Registrar isn't free to do anything he wants. Furthermore, the Trial Chamber at the ICC can even issue orders to ask the accused to actually contribute to his defence. So their system is obviously more sophisticated and of a better performance, but I hope that we'll find a solution so that you can benefit from the help of your associates, in accordance with our decision. Now, finally, Mr. Seselj, as you know, we still have six witnesses to hear, two who are scheduled for next week and then we'll have four left, four outstanding. If everything works according to plan, we should be finished with these witnesses in May. Then, according to Article 65 ter of the procedure, Rules of Procedure, the Defence must submit its 65 ter list. So now we have a legal question, and there's no decision on this. We need to know whether the burden of proof of the Prosecutor -- whether the Prosecution's case is rested or not, because we have the Court witnesses that are being heard in between. Normally, in Rule 85, we have evidence that is either the Prosecution's case or the Defence case, but it also says "unless decided otherwise by the Trial Chamber, in the interests of justice," which means that the Trial Chamber, in the interests of justice, has some leeway. We decided to ask for these Court witnesses to come in the interests of justice. Therefore, de jure, I believe that the Trial Chamber has not made a decision on this yet, but I believe that the Prosecution so far has no witnesses left. They can, of course, present new evidence. They can do that during the cross-examination of the witnesses. But he has no more witnesses on his list. So, Mr. Seselj, I would like to know whether you have already prepared your witness list, because we don't want to be in a situation where at the end of May -- or in May, we say, We're done with our witnesses, we have Rule 98 bis, but then we don't want you to ask us for two to three months to prepare your own list. So I'd like to know whether you've already -- whether you are preparing your list at the moment, even if you haven't actually written your list down completely. However, my fellow Judge Harhoff has something to say, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, I do have a few comments to what our authoritative Presiding Judge has just suggested. Now, first of all, in relation to the issue of the assistance to Mr. Krasic to cover his travel costs to The Hague, I really and honestly believe that this is a matter for the Registry to deal with, and not the Chamber, so I would be disinclined to go along with the Chamber addressing a letter directly to the Serbian authorities. I would find that highly inappropriate. But I did notice that at one point the Presiding Judge also mentioned -- and I don't know if that was a mistake, but you did, in fact, mention that we should address a letter to the Registrar, asking him to contact the ministry in Belgrade. Be that as it may, I do not think that it is appropriate for the Chamber, itself, to engage in any discussion with the Serbian authorities, or any other authorities, for that matter, in relation to the indigency of an accused. So this is at least to clarify my point of view. I have no observations regarding whether or not Mr. Karadzic is being treated differently, as I do not know this case, but I understand, and this is my recollection from last time we discussed this issue of the indigency of the accused in this case, you, Mr. Seselj, if my memory serves me right, the stumbling issue is whether or not you would be prepared to give information about the financial situation of your wife. And I think that your position was that you had given all the information about the financial situation relating to yourself, but that you refused to give any information in relation to your wife, and it was for that reason that the Registrar said that you had not fully co-operated with the Registry about your indigency, because full information would, in the Registrar's view, also involve your giving information about the financial status of your wife. Be that as it may, I have no further comments, except that if the difficulty here is that the Registrar is of the opinion that you have not -- still not fully co-operated with the Registry, then that appears to be different from what is actually going on in the Karadzic case, because I understand, without having any concrete knowledge about it, but I understand that Mr. Karadzic has, in fact, co-operated fully with the Registrar and has given all the information that the Registrar had asked for. In relation to the issue of your giving us your list of witnesses, my opinion is, and I think this is known -- this is well known to the Presiding Judge, that I do not think that we can ask an accused to reveal his list of witnesses before the Chamber has ruled in accordance with Rule 98 bis. That's the way I see it, because it would be, in my view, unfair to an accused to ask him to reveal his list of witnesses before the accused knows whether the Chamber has, in fact, accepted all the charges in the indictment. Chances are, of course, that a Chamber may decide to acquit the accused on some of the charges in the indictment; and if a Chamber, in fact, does so, and it has happened in this Tribunal, then, of course, the defendant need not bring any evidence relating to those counts. So I don't think that we can and, indeed, that we should ask you in advance. Of course, if you want to do it, it's your own choice. But I do not think that the Chamber can compel you to disclose your list of witnesses before we have given our oral decision on Rule 98 bis. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not just some, but, in fact, all counts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to answer the remarks just provided by Judge Harhoff. For one thing, I have not asked Mr. Seselj to provide this list. I have asked him whether he is thinking about this list and whether he's preparing it. Secondly, and more legally speaking, I could not disagree more. Article 65 ter says the following: "Following the presentation of the case of the Prosecution, and before the presentation of the case of the Defence, the Judge asked the Defence to present a list of witnesses." Now, my opinion is that the presentation of the means of the case of the Prosecution is finished. Article 65 ter (G) refers in no way to Article 98 bis, at no time does it refer to Article 98 bis. Hence, legally speaking, we could actually ask for the disclosure of this list, but I have no intention of forcing, through an interpretation of this rule. I just asked Mr. Seselj whether he is thinking about this list; that's all. I have not requested anything further. Now, on a second point, if the Chamber wishes to send a letter to the Serbian authorities, that's fine. If the Chamber doesn't want to, that's fine too. I will do it myself, personally, of my own initiative. That's what I want to do say. I find that we are in a situation -- in a totally blocked situation, and sending this problem back to the Registrar and leaving the accused to prove that he is, in fact, in a situation of indigency, will leave us stuck. I have only one solution, and if others agree with me about this solution, that's fine. And If they won't follow me, then I will have to do it alone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I merely want to say that I agree with the interpretation that Judge Harhoff just suggested. Before the presentation of the case of the Defence, we don't actually know if it will be presented or if, based on 98 bis or due to a decision of the accused, himself, whether there will be any need. So while we don't know if the case will, in fact, be tried or not, we cannot go further. On the issue of indigency and possible assistance to the Defence and concerning how indigency can be demonstrated, I also share Judge Harhoff's opinion that this is a matter to be determined by the Registry. But I am convinced that the accused will find some way of helping us out of this difficulty, of the situation in which we diverge on this matter, simply by giving us the few elements that are still in his possession, showing the Chamber that he is trying his best to co-operate. Perhaps, even today, he may have a few things to tell us about these matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Many issues have just been raised by all of you Judges. I'm going to provide you with a somewhat broader answer. First, as concerns Rule 98 bis, that Rule has been in existence for over 15 years, I would say, and it has undergone some changes in the meantime. Pursuant to that Rule, there was a time when a preliminary judgement was issued, and now a written decision is issued by a Trial Chamber, although the Rules of Evidence can be rejected, as all the charges has not been proven, and the criteria that are applied are the most favourable to the OTP. And when the final judgement is passed, then the criteria are applied that are most favourable for me, when all the evidence is valid. That's the difference between the application of Rule 98 bis and the final decision. It has never happened so far that an accused has been found not guilty pursuant to Rule 98 bis. What happened was that some charges were rejected, although I'm sure that here the OTP has not even remotely proven any of the charges. And if there were no pressures from outside of the Tribunal, I'm sure that a sentence could be passed according to Rule 98 bis, and that would also contain a ruling to give me compensation, together with the acquittal, for everything that I have suffered through my detention. That possibility exists in any other courts. Unfortunately, at this Tribunal, this has never happened. All the Rules are violated here, and nothing is possible here. Therefore, I'm sure that there is no single piece of evidence, and if there is not too much pressure from the outside, that your rule, according to Rule 98 bis, will be acquittal already in May. However, I'm aware how much the Western powers don't want to see me back in Serbia. They have come like a ton of bricks on my party. They have not managed to destroy it, although they have damaged it considerably. But it is still -- it is already recovering. And my return to Serbia would contribute to that recovery. Since, in the eyes of America, I am still a danger if I return to Serbia; I'm also dangerous for the European Union, England, France -- France which is still meddling with the internal affairs of Serbia. Look at what they're doing in Pristina. They will do everything possible to prevent my return, even by launching physical attacks on the members of the Trial Chamber, who are trying to use their judgement in passing their decisions. This is my realistic concern, but we will see how things will look like. However, if that decision, according to Rule 98 bis, is not for acquittal, Your Honours, do not think that I can start my case in a month or two. The OTP needed five years to prepare for these proceedings from the moment I was arrested. Since I personally am at least twice as clever and as capable as the entire OTP, I will not need five years, but I will need at least two years before I start presenting my case. I have still not started working on my case, because I've not had the resources, I've not had the money. My associates are scattered. They haven't been paid for seven years. So you will have to give me at least two years to be able to prepare my case, and that on the condition that all the other problems are resolved. Over a year ago, I promised that I would no longer mention the issue of financing. I gave up on that, because I realised that all the doors were closed. You, yourselves, Your Honours, have raised the issue, and that's why I'm going to tell you a few things. In 2003, I provided information about my financial situation, and I gave that to the Registrar by signing a form. Whatever I could report, I did. I reported everything. I disclosed all my assets. The Registrar is now asking for my wife, my sister, to disclose their assets. They did that with my mother previously, and so on and so forth. Who of you, Your Honours, would be willing and in a position to provide somebody with information about the assets of their spouses without their consent? My wife does not want to give me that information. What can I do? Shall I beat my wife? I'm from the Balkans, so maybe you think that it would be most appropriate and befitting. However, I'm not that much of a man from the Balkans. And there's also a danger, if I beat her, that she will pay me back. I've been in prison for seven years. My wife wasn't. And God knows who would fare worse in such a potential skirmish. So you're asking me for something that I can't do, I can't provide.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If this is not too much meddling in your business, just tell me so and I will ask you to no more of an answer than that. But is it so that in Yugoslavia there are two systems for the management of your financial estate, two possible ways in which the estate is shared out between the husband and the wife? Is it possible for your estate to be separate between you and your wife and/or for your estate to be one? And have you, if there are two such possibilities, have you made a choice? I'm not asking you which choice you made, but is it possible to make such a choice, and have you made such a choice, in accordance with the legislation in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Judge, under the Serbian law there is no more Yugoslavia, because I believe you mentioned Yugoslavia. It's been long gone. So under the Serbian law, each person has his or her own assets. The only assets shared are those gained jointly, something that is jointly purchased, jointly gained or earned. If we're looking at real estate, my wife has a piece of real estate which is not particularly valuable or expensive, whereas I, myself, have nothing, nothing at all. I have been without a source of earnings for the last seven years. All my assets were in my bank account back in Belgrade. I have nothing. It's been emptied and spent. I have three young children, one son who is a grown-up, and that son does not have a job. I also have two grandchildren. Therefore, this is all perfectly clear. Secondly, the Registrar has a team of investigators. All doors are open to them over in Belgrade. That team has had plenty of time to establish anything they liked. I declared my bank account in New York, which goes back to 1989. It is actually 21 years' old. May that be noted. There was 70.000 dollars in that account. That account was blocked as of five or six years ago. I tried to use the services of the Serbian embassy to find out why that account was blocked. As you know, I was not a fugitive at any point. They did not provide a direct answer; rather, they said that I would still be able to use the money to pay for the services of an American lawyer who would be representing me before this Tribunal. As you well know, it would never even cross my mind to hire the services of an American lawyer. So what now? Nothing much. Everything is as it was. The Registrar is well able to establish anything they like, yet they refuse to. I provided appropriate information. It is up to them to actually check. They should come forward and say if any of my information is accurate, but the Registrar deliberately avoids doing just that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You know very well that it is up to you to prove indigency. You can't simply say that the Registrar has the means at its disposal to find the information it wants. It is actually for you to give that information.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no court in the entire world that has a registry this powerful. Here, the Registrar makes decisions about my Defence; they make decisions as to who I would be legally represented by. Where on earth can you find a court of law allowing something like that? I have proven already that I had no money to fund my defence, yet the Registrar is telling me that I have failed to prove it. So what can I do? Is the Registrar always right? No, I think sometimes the Registrar has been known to tell a lie, on many an occasion during my case. There were different people filling that post, but the institution remains. I say I have nothing, and they claim that I have something. Are we going to go on like that until the end of time? Nevertheless, I have not worked on the Defence case so far. What I have been doing is preparing, to the best of my ability, under exceptionally difficult circumstances. I've been preparing to refute any claims made by the Prosecution's false witnesses. I'm not unhappy. I believe I have been reasonably successful. I would have been far more successful had I not been hampered in my work by the various extrajudicial obstacles, had I not been hampered in terms of working with my associates, and a number of other obstacles that were laid in my way. If I do not get any funds for my defence from the International Tribunal, that will simply leave me unable to put forward a Defence case. In order to fund my Defence case, some things must be paid up front, and that means the pre-trial stage as well as the trial, itself. The Registrar must be able to establish to what extent I'm able to chip in, in terms of funding my defence, and to what extent I'm not. There are various criteria. Let's look at the costs of defence cases in all the other trials before the International Tribunal and compare. Let's look at the chronology. The pre-trial stage over a total of five years for my category, and this is category 3 or class 3, there was a break lasting 18 months, and the cost was 380.000, and then that goes up to 24 months, at most. My pre-trial stage took five years. Just look at my expenses. I had to get rid of a lawyer who had been imposed on me in front of the Dutch Bar, and then I had to look into some information in relation to the first Serb lawyer who was imposed on me as a stand-by. Someone must foot the bill, and it simply has to be the International Tribunal. I would not have incurred all those bills had all those situations not been foisted on me by illegal means and methods. So much for the funding. Now, as regards my legal counsel, as we speak, I only have one with whom I'm enjoying privileged communication, Boris Aleksic. I'm very happy with the work that he's been doing, exceptionally happy. You've seen for yourselves he writes very good submissions and he is a very competent lawyer. I'm also happy with my case assistant, Marina Raguz. She's not a lawyer, herself, but she has proven to be quite good at writing submissions. Nevertheless, I cannot go on without Zoran Krasic. Zoran Krasic has been with me throughout, from the word go, and he knows this case. He has been on this case for the last seven years. It is, however, impossible for me to work with him because his status here before this Tribunal is simply humiliating. You must realise one thing. He knows about all these protected witnesses. He knows about all the confidential information and documents. He's seen it all. There is nothing knew that could possibly turn up here without him having access to it. Over the last seven years, he has simply studied it all. Why the whole thing, then? We move into closed session, and he's expected to leave the courtroom, quite aside from what I actually believe about the closed sessions during the Defence case and how that will happen. Unless the OTP stages some sort of a show again, all of my witnesses will be testifying live, in public, viva voce. That happens to be the only kind of evidence that I recognise as legitimate. I don't recognise the evidence as defined by a continental law or, indeed, a common law. This is a criminal case and not a civil case. Everything must be said in open court. We want to avoid situations of people writing stuff that somebody allegedly said, yet not knowing that this is the case. This is something that must not be allowed to happen in a criminal case like this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, you remember the reasons very well. There is no need to remind you of them here. You know what the reasons are for the Registry's decision to suspend Mr. Krasic's situation, and these reasons have not changed. This Chamber can do nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I simply cannot settle for that, the fact that the Registrar can suspend my legal counsel. I will never settle for that, I will never come to terms with that. It cannot be the case. Secondly, you suspended my legal counsel based on a suspicion of the OTP that he was exerting pressure on witnesses. Why was that never proven? It was first presented over two years ago, and it hasn't been proven. Will Zoran Krasic remain branded for the rest of his life just because there was at one point a suspicion on the part of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, there's a mistake in the transcript. Page 21, line 4, "you have suspended my legal counsel." The Chamber has suspend nobody. We did not do that. The Registry did that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have not received the interpretation of what you have just said, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was trying to say that there is a mistake in the transcript. Page 21, line 4, it says "you suspended my legal counsel." The Chamber wishes to point out that we did nothing of the sort. The Registry suspended, not the Chamber. So when you say "you," you mean this Tribunal or the Registry, but it is not the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Mr. President, when I say "you," normally I mean the Tribunal as a whole, which I view as a single institution. You have large-scale machinery here taking on too many powers, and sometimes the Registrar appears to be more powerful than the Trial Chambers themselves, which is not the case anywhere else in the world. Nevertheless, what exactly is the problem we're dealing with here? This is something that you acknowledged in your last ruling, for Zoran Krasic to remain in this half-suspended condition, as it were. He can work with me as far as matters of public record are concerned, but not those that are confidential or outside the public eye. So, for example, he comes and visits me in the Detention Unit. That means that all the conversations will be listened to, or they will tape him with a camera, like the last time he came. They took us to a room that was bugged, and they continually recorded all of our conversations. Why would, then, he visit me if I do not enjoy the privilege of confidential communication? Or maybe there will be a representative of the Tribunal sitting there listening to our conversations, and that is exactly what the lawyers here did to me when I was providing them with instructions as to how to represent me before the Bar here in Holland in June 2006. Throughout all this time, the Detention Unit interpreter was there listening to our conversation. Well, that is one thing that I will be having. If Zoran Krasic visits me, then there has to be privileged communication, not being eavesdropped or anything like that. He's searched every time he enters the Detention Unit, and that, I think, is quite sufficient. At any rate, Your Honours, in February the dead-line expired for you to receive a report on the real condition of Witness 008, the false Witness 008. I have not received a report yet. I'm not sure whether you have. This was a chance for you to see how witnesses were instrumentalised by the OTP for the purposes of this case and how they came to be in the courtroom. I have another legal counsel. This is Dejan Mirovic, who holds an MA degree in Law. He's helping me in my contempt case. He helped me the first time around, and I have now submitted another application to the Registrar for him to be taken on for my next case. There is another vacant spot on my legal team. At the beginning, there were three of them. I would like to fill that post by hiring Mirovic another MA in Law, Zoran Krasic, Boris Aleksic, and Dejan Mirovic. That would be my team, these three prominent and well-regarded lawyers. If needed, I can file a written motion to the Registrar in order to see to it that this is done. Dejan Mirovic will also be helping me and representing me in the contempt case. That's is as far as my legal counsel and my legal team are concerned. So far, they have not received a cent, not a penny, for their work. I have been able to cover some efforts for them, but now I find myself unable to do even that. They haven't been to see me for quite some time, and, frankly, I don't know if and when they will. There's another problem that I'm facing which will make it impossible for me to present my Defence case unless dealt with in good time. If we think back to what Mr. Slobodan Milosevic actually had during his trial, is something that I see as the bare minimum. I will not go below that. I will not settle for any less than that. When the OTP case was concluded, during the actual OTP case Milosevic enjoyed the aid of legal assistants and counsel who would normally wait for him in a special room outside the courtroom every time a session drew to a close, and then they would talk, confer, and so on and so forth. When the Milosevic case was done, Mr. Milosevic was granted a special office in the Detention Unit in which he had access to a telephone line and a fax machine. He was allowed to use the phone as much as he liked, and he was allowed to make all the calls he liked. Whoever is preparing for a Defence case must keep numerous communication lines open to a great many people. 90 per cent of the calls normally come to nothing, but then there is that 1 per cent which normally comes back with a result. Nevertheless, there must be access to these services, and Mr. Milosevic enjoyed that access. The Detention Unit authorities now refuse to issue their permission for something like that to be arranged for me. They have now awarded an office for Mr. Tolimir, Mr. Karadzic, and me to be used jointly. There is a telephone line in that room, but we were officially told that we could use this telephone, in terms of privileged communication, only by using the same number -- dialing the same number that we normally dial from the corridor of the Detention Unit. And that number is normally related to a particular legal counsel we are hiring. Anything else we do, we must buy a card, pay for the conversation ourselves, and these conversations are normally eavesdropped on. Now, this is something that I simply find myself unable to accept. Secondly, we have at different stages in these proceedings. The Tolimir trial has just started; the Karadzic trial has just started; and I am expected to commence my Defence case. What do I need this office for? I need this office to see potential witnesses there. I may have, let's say, 60 or 70 witnesses appearing. I will need to see at least 500 or 600 of those before I pick the witnesses who would eventually -- who would eventually appear. That is precisely what Mr. Milosevic did. He didn't bring all of the 2.000 witnesses here to see them, but he did have a list containing as many as 2.000 names. Every time he picked a witness, he would be given an opportunity to talk to them three or four times before the witness ever entered the courtroom. For example, take my case. He spoke to me a total of four times, because I appeared as one of his Defence witnesses. And he was using, for that purpose, this office. And the meetings were attended also by Dr. Branko Rakic, his legal counsel, Mr. Milosevic, himself, and me. And there was no supervision going on whatsoever. Knowing that Mr. Milosevic enjoyed this privilege, well, then certainly I must as well until the moment I die. This is the only way it can happen; no other way but this way. That is as far as the conditions for preparing my Defence case are concerned. Problem number 4, which is exceptionally important, this is something that I've drawn your attention to previously. At one point during the pre-trial stage, I filed a number of motions to the Trial Chamber, more than once, at any rate, as far as I remember, about the following: I suggested that a number of different intelligence services, American, British, German, French, Croatian, and the Muslim Intelligence Service in Bosnia, be subpoenaed in order to force them to submit all of their intelligence reports, all of their information, all of their Official Notes containing a mention or a reference to my name. The Trial Chamber came back to me, saying that I had to get the work done myself, that I should try to get hold of these documents, and then should I fail, they would be ruling on that. My legal counsel followed this course of action. It was Mr. Aleksandar Vucic who at the time was in charge of dealing with that. He dispatched requests to the US Intelligence Service, the French Intelligence Service, the Dutch -- the Italian Intelligence Service, and the German Intelligence Service. No response came from anyone but the US Intelligence Service, and they wanted the costs covered. I forwarded their response to the Tribunal. I am unable to use my legal assistants to address the Croat authorities or, indeed, the Muslim authorities. Therefore, this should be done directly by the Tribunal. This information is essential to me. It is material to my Defence case. Unless I get hold of this information in good time, I really have no idea how I should be presenting my Defence case, as a whole. In the OTP's case, they got everything they wanted from anyone they wanted. They carefully picked what documents exactly would be made available to me from the archives and from all over the place. But then, mutatis mutandis, I must get access to everything wherever my name is mentioned, so then I can pick, myself, whether I will be using a document in the courtroom or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, on this latter point that I no longer had in mind, I followed closely what was said in the Karadzic case, where he also asked the states to communicate a number of elements, and I remember what the German ambassador said. He said as far as secret services are concerned, this comes under state secret, and it's impossible to disclose anything. Now, regarding the other countries which participated, they're willing to answer as long as they are given a very clear explanation about the purpose of the request. They don't want to contribute to fishing for information and nothing else. So I believe that your -- you probably will not have a positive answer. I didn't know that your associate had written to everyone, that you only got an answer from the Americans, who were asking you to pay for these documents. I guess that's what they were asking you to do.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Americans were willing, at least on the face of it, to meet my request. However, they had a price list for that. They were prepared to provide documents at a price, and they explained the costs -- the costs of the staff, photocopying, and so on and so forth. However, it seems that all states but Serbia are entitle to have their state secrets. Only from Serbia, Karadzic documents were provided to the Tribunal. Even if some documents were missing, they were produced there and then in order to meet the requests of the OTP. There was such cases. In the proceedings against the six who were tried for alleged crimes on Kosovo, I know for a fact that certain documents were produced subsequently in order to meet the requirements of the OTP; documents which were not authentic. Those documents were forged subsequently in order to prove some things. Serbia has provided everything, nobody else does, because there's always an axe hanging over Serbia. The other countries do not treat this Tribunal as a serious court of law. Americans, for example, their state interest has always been above the Tribunal. If this, indeed, is an international tribunal, then the interests of this Tribunal has to be above any individual state interest, especially in view of the fact that it is very difficult to prove here that a state is interested in hiding documents. The real interests of Western powers, such as America, Italy, France, is to cover documents that refer to me. And all that is done only to make my defence more difficult. I am sure that all the documents that mention my name and that are kept in their archives would be exculpatory for me. Their intelligence services were involved in all war events. They have precise information. And that information is contradictory to the statements issued by their politicians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, let me remind you of the law. Our Rule 54 bis solves this problem. A party, i.e., you, asking for a -- i.e., a party requesting an order on Rule 54 that say produce document and so forth, will identify the documents, if possible, to indicate how they are relevant to any matter in the issue before the Judge. 3 explains the steps that have been made by the applicant to secure the state's assistance. This is Rule 54 bis(A)(i) to (iii). "The Judge of the Trial Chamber will reject an application if it is satisfied that the documents are not relevant, that no reasonable steps have been made by the applicants to obtain the documents or the information from the state." This is Rule 54 bis(B)(1)(ii), and the decision of the Trial Chamber can be appealed. So the procedure is extremely clear. If you want, for example, the German Secret Services to communicate documents to you, well, first you have to ask for them. And if you get no answer, then you can make a written submission, explaining what the relevance of these documents is, and, secondly, what steps have you taken so far, and, three, what is the exact nature of the document. The procedure is stated in Rule 54 bis. You have to follow it. And I believe that this is exactly what Mr. Karadzic did. He followed the procedure, Rule 54 bis.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is exactly what I've done. As for the nature of these documents, I would say that they deal with my activities during the war. My name is mentioned in all of them, and that should be a good enough reason for me to request those documents covering a period from 1991 to 19 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I believe that at one point in time in your country you were vice-prime minister, and you dealt with your own secret services. So you know exactly how they work, how they operate. They're secret by nature. So they don't disclose much. If you're waiting for miracles, well, you know it's a hard road to follow, but you can always try. You might eventually obtain something.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, when I was the vice-president of my government, whatever I requested from Serbian and Yugoslav intelligence services, I got all that, by and large. Many of those documents later on, when I was no longer the vice-president of the government, I disclosed all of them. Once, they wanted to put me on trial for disclosing an official secret, but they soon changed their mind. I even managed to get hold of my entire police record. There were no big secrets for me there. And here you could also see that I had much better documents at my disposal than the OTP, and I'm always able to lift the mask of the false documents that the OTP is trying to pass on me. There we've seen documents that were not signed, they didn't have a stamp on them, they were not recorded, and so on and so forth. As far as the foreign services are concerned, I'm powerless here. I don't have the money to pay the Americans. And the rest are keeping quiet. And as for Croatia, I can't even talk to them. I don't have anybody to be my mediator. I personally don't want to do that; My legal advisers don't want to do that. Aleksandar Vucic didn't want to do it originally, but then I learned later on that he travelled to Zagreb on several occasions. And when I learned that, I had already dismissed him. I really don't know why he travelled to Zagreb, who he meant there, and what connections he had there, and what things he was involved in there. In any case, my assistance team has always been under scrutiny, and you realised what that scrutiny resulted in. The team has been changed. I'm not complaining. I have expected all those blows, and I've managed to put through all those blows, not only in biological terms but also in political terms. In political terms, for America and its allies, I am currently more dangerous than I ever was seven years ago. And they are still not happy about my possible return to Belgrade. So we will still have an opportunity to engage in this tug-of-war for seven or eight years, at least until all this is over. But I'm not complaining, I'm not complaining. I'm just telling you that I will not give up an inch of my rights and principles that I adhere to. And I'm telling you, though, these proceedings cannot be finished that easily and at my expense. I appreciate that it will eventually be at my expense, but in the meantime I will be able to deal a lot of counter-blows to my enemies and my opponents. As my -- a friend of mine used to say, I'm not a squirrel; I can't be treated like this by just anybody. I -- you should, rather, compare me with a dragon. That would be a much better comparison. And I have a minor issue, or minor on the face of it. It's a very concrete issue, and I believe it's important enough for me to inform you about it. There is an agency called SENSE. SENSE Tribunal is its full name. Its sponsors are The Hague Tribunal also the European Commission, the governments of the Netherlands, Luxembourg, and Germany, and the Source Open Society Foundation. That agency falsifies information from the proceedings that are conducted before this Tribunal. And last time, the week before last, when we heard the protected witness, Ms. Biersay mentioned or quoted my statement that I issued at a press conference in 1992, and that was when I requested for Ostoja Sibincic and others to be released after having been arrested in Hrtkovci. The SENSE Agency, or the SENSE, whatever its name is, published as follows: "Ms. Biersay quoted Seselj's statement at a press conference held in 1993, at which he requested for the detained activeness of the Serbian Radical Party to be released, including Sibincic." This means that somebody suggested that that agency should infiltrate a piece of false information, and that was that I treated Sibincic as a member of the Serbian Radical Party, although at that conference, I said - and I published that in my book "Bila Bandic Has to Fall" - the Serbian Radical Party, that is the third issue that I would -- we would like to communication our position. The Serbian Radical Party requests the release of Sobija Ilicic [phoen] and others who were arrested in Sovislavici [phoen], former Hrtkovci, because we believe that they have been arrested because of their political campaign or, rather, a political campaign conducted by some circles of the federal authorities, primarily Tibor Varadi, a minister and official of the Pro Ustasha Party of the Yugoslav Association for Democratic Initiative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I believe the accused is raising an issue of evidence rather than an administrative issue at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is evidence, Mr. Seselj, this is evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, this is an administrative issue, not an issue of evidence. I would like to -- I'm trying to show you how a propaganda war is waged against me by the SENSE Agency, supported by the Tribunal. And then I go -- I went on to say if somebody committed a crime, it is up to a court to establish that, and I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, I'm sure that you know the media better than I do. You can send them some mail, you know, a letter, to ask them to amend their press release, and they'll make the amendment. They might have made a mistake. I don't know. I didn't follow this. You can always write to them so that they can make a correction.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was convinced that you, as members of the Trial Chamber, will be very interested in learning about this problem. I sent a submission to the Registry, and that submission was prepared by Boris Aleksic. But I would like to also inform you about the forgeries that I'm dealing with. I have been dealing with such forgeries all the time. And could you please allow me to read two more sentences and quote what I said at the conference, and how the two sentences have been misinterpreted by the SENSE. I said if somebody committed a crime, it has to be confirmed by a court. They were arrested after a political campaign, without a piece of evidence that a crime was, indeed, committed. We demand that they be released and that they be allowed to mount a defence at large. If anybody has to be arrested, it should be those who committed the most atrocious -- such a crime, and exchange them with the Croats. And then I went on to talk about how those criminals were released, and that was in 1992, and it's clear what I wanted to say. At the same time, the SENSE Agency published that on that occasion I protected members of the Serbian Radical Party, although on several occasions we established here in this place that they were not members of the Serbian Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The accused is clearly continuing to present evidence. He's making a submission about evidence that was presented to you in court. He's making an argument as to why some evidence that has been presented is wrong based on some documents he's reading from. If the accused intends to turn this into an evidentiary hearing, then we should have this piece of evidence that he's reading from admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, regarding this agency, this is not the first time that there are some technical problems, and I say, quote/unquote, "technical problems" with this agency. You're not the first accused contesting what this agency is saying. But they can answer any request made by you, and if they made a mistake, because they can make mistakes, well, they will correct their mistake. Jumping to conclusions by saying that they're forging the truth or giving false true, that's going a bit too far. Let me tell you that we have been in contact for years now, and it's the first time that you are addressing this problem of this SENSE Agency. It's up to you to solve the problem. We're not here to deny freedom of speech to anyone. We're not here to tell anyone, You are not reflecting correctly what is being said during the hearings. It is not our job; it is not what we're here for.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in my view, your job is anything to do with this trial and my position in it. You are the guardians of the just nature of this trial. As I told you, I submitted this to the Registry, and the Registry's in charge of working with this agency, in charge of funding the work of the agency. I officially submitted this to the Registrar. I'm merely now informing you that I, in fact, did that and why; which concludes the matter for me. That is all I had to say in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You're telling us that you made a submission to the Registrar, and you will -- it's up to the Registry to decide. Mr. Marcussen, before we wind up, do you have anything to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I do have a few points. First of all, and this goes to the issue of what stage the proceedings is in, the issue came up about whether or not the Prosecution's case is closed. As I indicated last time we were in court and this issue came up, it's the Prosecution's position that the Prosecution's part of the presentation of evidence is not yet over. In addition to issues that might come up during the witnesses - and I understand that the President has already deal with this, and I accept, of course, the position that there can be Prosecution exhibits tendered during that -- during the testimony of the remaining witnesses - I also wanted to alert the Trial Chamber to the fact that the Prosecution intend to file another motion for admission of documents from the Bar table. We will make a short request for leave to exceed the word limits, on the basis of -- for the same reasons that we sought it for the first Bar table motion. We will get that filed very quickly. We just need to finalise some technical issues, and then we can file that. On the 23rd of April, 2002, Mr. Mundis -- no, that cannot be right. 2008, my apologies. Mr. Mundis indicated that the Prosecution was working on preparing a list of additional videos to be shown. We would like to show a few more videos to the Court. We have considerably cut down the list, so I think we could do a short video session, but we would like to present some further videos. And as the Court has decided that the propose procedure is that the videos be shown in court, we would need some time to do that. So those were the first two things in relation to the close of the Prosecution case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, a spur of the moment. I am just finding out about these videos. You know that we still have six witnesses, and you could always show these six -- these witnesses [as interpreted] during the hearing of these six witnesses in the framework of the time allotted to you; for VS-1058, for example, through VS-1058, because having a special video session would mean that you would be allotted additional time, and personally I would be against that. I can tell thank you immediately. So if you have a few videos to show, since we're going to have witnesses, use these witnesses to show your videos, you know, during your cross. Say, Mr. Seselj said this earlier, I will show you a video, and then we'll see the video. That way, you can obtain what you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm not certain that the remaining witnesses can speak to the particular witness -- to the particular videos that we have left, so I'm not sure that's feasible. And on the issue of time, I believe that the Prosecution had five hours and something left of its time before the remaining witnesses were converted into Court witnesses, so I would think that we have some time. In any event, all we need is maybe an hour or two hours. It's -- we are not talking about a massive amount of videos to present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, I'm not convinced that you still have five hours. Our Legal Officers have checked this closely, and I don't think that you have five hours left. We'll take a close look at this to see exactly how much time you have left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, as for the issue of the accused's ability to present his defence, the way I have heard the accused speak today, he has essentially said he does not have the resources and, therefore, is not capable of preparing his defence. That, again, raises the issue of whether or not it is required for the Trial Chamber to impose counsel, and it's a difficult situation for the Trial Chamber, I realise. And I also note that although I'm not to make any submissions on whether or not the Serbian authorities should or should not be requested to provide information, the Prosecution would request that the Trial Chamber, if it is to make such a request to Serbia, clarifies to the Prosecution and to the accused whether or not the request has been made, because the Trial Chamber has found that the accused is not able to ensure his defence without some legal assistance of some sort. So that's what I wanted to say on this point. I would also note that the accused made a lot of arguments about how he had prevented from doing this or how he didn't have resources. I think it's important to put on record as well, though, that the accused has actually presented, with various of his motions, quite a lot of witness statements he as obtained actually even before the commencement of the trial. And as we have frequently debated, when various witnesses have been cross-examined, he has obviously had the resources to have somebody collect various pieces of evidence for him and have them faxed to him in court. And I put this on record because I think that it's important that the public is informed about what's going on here. And when the accused is presenting himself as some sort of a victim of the system here, I think it is inappropriate. The Trial Chamber has done what it could and been very, very lax in allowing the accused to present his evidence during the trial, has allowed him not to provide documents in translated form, has allowed him to come with the documents late. So I think important that the record is somehow made as to what the accused's ability is to present his case. So, Your Honours, I think it's important, as we move forward, that we clarify the accused's position on this counsel issue. And I would note that once the Defence case starts, it will be important, of course, for the fairness of the trial and for the Prosecution's ability to cross-examine remaining witnesses, that we do get things translated, that we do get them on time. So if the accused is not able to respect reasonable dead-lines for those kind of things once the Defence case starts, the whole issue of his ability to present his defence comes up again. And the issue of whether or not he can do so without some sort of legal assistance, unfortunately, will arise again, but this time in a new form. But it cannot end up being the case that the Prosecution's ability to prepare for cross-examination of witnesses get prejudiced because the accused refuses to provide information to the Registrar which enables the Registrar to give him counsel, if that's what actually is needed. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, we only have five minutes to go before the tape finishes, quite, but we must finish now. We have five minutes, Mr. Seselj, and then we will wind up.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just respond to Mr. Marcussen. As for the admission of documents into evidence, what Mr. Marcussen has announced is impossible. Any documents had to be tendered while the witnesses were around, while he was examining his witnesses, now the Chamber's witnesses, and potential Defence witnesses. The only thing that can be admitted directly into evidence with no witnesses are photocopies of portions of my books or the pieces that I wrote. This is the only thing that can be Bar-tabled, as it were. The other thing. Mr. Marcussen has just stated something that is utter nonsense. If I have no funding to present my Defence case, then obviously this brings up the issue of my lawyer. What exactly will this lawyer be doing, presenting a Defence case against my will? I don't see any brains here. Do you have any, sir? How on earth could a lawyer like that be allowed to do that? Milosevic was tricked some time ago. He submitted a witness list, and then a lawyer was imposed on him to pick witnesses from that list. That didn't work. Me, I will not be forwarding to you a Defence witness list, or, indeed, any of my evidence until I have received sufficient funds to appropriately present Defence case. A budget must be determined for my Defence case in relation to the pre-trial stage, in relation to the OTP case, and in relation to the Defence case; the breakdown being like that. A budget is determined based on the complexity level of the case, and then we can say, I can fund this or that portion from such and such sources, but the rest of the bill should be footed by the International Tribunal, that being the only legitimate method of going about this. No one so far here has even tried to determine a budget for my defence or, indeed, to ascertain what, if any, of these expenses I can cover myself and from what sources. And yet you would like to assign a lawyer to me. Are you in your right state of mind, people? How exactly are you going to do that? If you're bringing a fool into this courtroom, and this fool will be travelling around Serbia, tracking down witnesses. Well, this fool appointed by you would never be allowed to enter Serbia, let alone pick my witnesses. Maybe someone from this OTP of yours, some of their staff, maybe they should go, have a walk around, and then tell other people there that I'm probably the most heinous person alive. Am I the worst person you've ever met? I'm sure you've never met anyone like me throughout your careers, not you, not the Trial Chamber. I don't think you've ever met anyone like this before. You are bound to get a lot more headaches because I'm here. I will not give up any of my claims, and I'm ready to stake my life to stand up for my rights and principles. You are powerless when you face me, and my power is enormous. My greatest resources are right here between my ears, and I'm sure, Mr. Marcussen, that you've had ample opportunity to see for yourself. You can't overcome that. There's no one available to do the work for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, we're about to close. And, anyhow, we're running ahead of things, because we still have to deal with 98 bis. And if there's one thing that I'm sure I understand, is that you are asking for two years to prepare yourself. This much, I understand. Until now, that was not clear to me. Secondly, you are asking for financial means in order to fund the presentation of your witnesses. Now, this is another element that the Chamber will keep in mind when they make decisions. We will meet again next week. I can't remember if it will be morning hearings or afternoon hearings, but, anyhow, you will be told. We have VS-1058 and Gasi, one and a half hours for the Chamber, one and a half hours for the OTP, one and a half hours for Mr. Seselj, followed the next morning by Mr. Gasic [as interpreted], who has 30 minutes. In theory, only issues related to his testimony will be raised, and no administrative issues, because that would be a waste of time. That's what I want to tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, Judge Harhoff, who has a very vast experience in these matters, is pointing out to us that when we start on the presentation of the Defence case, a new financial regime comes into place. What you might want to do is discuss this with the Registry people who visit at the Detention Unit. Mr. Petrov is about to change his position. Somebody's going to replace him, Ms. Campbell, and you should take it up with her. See if you can solve this problem. She is the person you can talk to in the coming weeks, in the coming days, because we are now moving into a different phase with a different financial regime. You have to bring your witnesses; you have to see your witnesses. We have to pay the planes, and the hotels, and the meals for your witnesses. This is obvious, without question. Now, we will stop here, because we are running ahead of ourselves. I think it was a good idea to mention your list of witnesses, because we were able to sketch out what problems you were going to be faced with in the time to come. We will meet again next week. It will be afternoon hearings, Judge Harhoff just told us, and we will meet, therefore, at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 9th day of March, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.55 p.m.,
